summary.routeReason: A managed OAuth app exists in Composio's managed OAuth directory, but for external users who add a bot to their own servers you need your own app: the consent screen would otherwise show Composio's app, and the bot identity, permissions and rate-limit quota are tied to the app you register. Discord's docs describe registering your own developer application and retrieving client ID and secret as the first step ["S1"], and the bot token is generated when you create a bot user in the Developer Portal ["S8"].

managedOAuth.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Discord, so you can test and launch without registering one. Bring your own app to show your name on the consent screen, request custom scopes, or get a separate rate-limit quota.

summary.difficultyReason: Registering an app, enabling the bot, choosing minimal permissions and testing in a test server is straightforward ["S11"], but reading message content requires the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent, which must be toggled and later approved once the app passes 10,000 unique users ["S5"]["S9"].

testingBeforeReview.text: Apps can keep using intents and join servers while a privileged intent review is pending, so testing can happen before and during review.

mainBlocker.text: Reading users' messages requires the MESSAGE_CONTENT privileged intent, which must be enabled and, above the user threshold, approved by Discord.

summary.nextAction: Create your application in the Discord Developer Portal (https://discord.com/developers/applications), then on the Bot page add a bot user and copy the bot token.

activeWork.text: Estimate: About 1-2 hours to register the app, add the bot, set installation contexts and default install settings (bot scope plus Send Messages and Read Message History permissions), enable the MESSAGE_CONTENT intent, and test in a test server; more if you later need to write privileged intent review answers.

reviewWait.text: Provider does not publish a turnaround we could verify.

policyDeadlines.text: If the app passes 10,000 unique users with a privileged intent enabled, you have 90 days from the notification to apply for access.
Privileged intent access must be reapplied for annually after approval.

summary.routeReason: Composio's managed OAuth directory does offer a managed Notion OAuth app, but for external customers you likely want your own app: a public connection gives you your own consent-screen identity, your own capability selection, and your own rate-limit quota instead of sharing Composio's. Notion also lets you create and use a public connection without a Marketplace listing, so bringing your own app is feasible without review.

managedOAuth.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Notion, so you can test and launch without registering one. Bring your own app to show your name on the consent screen, request custom scopes, or get a separate rate-limit quota.

summary.difficultyReason: The OAuth flow itself is standard and can be started as soon as client credentials and redirect URI are configured, but you must choose installation scope correctly at creation (it cannot be changed), implement server-side code exchange and refresh-token storage, and handle per-user page sharing and rate limits.

testingBeforeReview.text: You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration's client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review is not required.

mainBlocker.text: Each user must individually authorize and pick pages, and only that user can then interact with the connection, so multi-member workspaces need per-user consent.

summary.nextAction: Create a new connection in the Notion Developer portal (Build → Connections), set installation scope to Any workspace, add your HTTPS redirect URI, and select the Read content and Insert content capabilities.

activeWork.text: Estimate: About 2-4 hours to register the public connection, configure redirect URIs and capabilities, implement the authorize/callback/token-exchange and refresh flow, and store tokens securely; more if you also prepare a Marketplace listing.

reviewWait.text: Provider does not publish a turnaround we could verify.

policyDeadlines.text: Free workspace block limit takes effect on September 8, 2026, which may affect workspaces your users connect.

steps.title: Create a public connection
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, Build → Connections → Create new connection. Enter name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), and choose installation scope Any workspace for external users.

steps.title: Select minimal capabilities
steps.detail: Choose Read content and Insert content only — enough to read and create pages, nothing more.
steps.outcome: Capabilities limited to reading and creating pages.

steps.title: Retrieve client credentials
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and client secret; store the secret server-side only.
steps.outcome: Client ID and secret available to your server.

steps.title: Implement authorize redirect
steps.detail: Send users to the Notion authorization URL with owner=user, client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code.
steps.outcome: Users can start the consent flow.

steps.title: Exchange code for tokens on server
steps.detail: POST the temporary code to the token endpoint with client credentials and redirect_uri; store access_token and refresh_token securely.
steps.outcome: Per-user tokens stored and usable for API calls.

steps.title: Implement token refresh
steps.detail: Use the refresh_token to obtain a new access_token and new refresh_token, and persist both.
steps.outcome: Long-lived access without re-consent.

steps.title: Test read and create in a test workspace
steps.detail: Authorize with a test account, pick pages in the page picker, then call Retrieve and Create page endpoints.
steps.outcome: Confirmed read and create work with granted pages.

steps.title: Handle rate limits and errors
steps.detail: Respect Retry-After on 429s and surface rate_limit_reason; retry only appropriate responses.
steps.outcome: Robust behavior under per-connection and per-workspace limits.

steps.title: Ship OAuth flow to customers
steps.detail: Expose the authorize link to external users; each user authorizes individually and shares chosen pages.
steps.outcome: External users can connect their workspaces.

steps.title: Optional: submit Marketplace listing
steps.detail: If you want discovery, create a listing in the Marketplace dashboard and submit for review; listing is optional.
steps.outcome: Listing submitted or deliberately skipped.

steps.title: Monitor and rotate credentials
steps.detail: Track rate-limit health, rotate secrets, and revoke tokens no longer used.
steps.outcome: Ongoing secure operation.
